GK11-q01-y6c4fs: 10 seconds is too short; even a single track takes at least 14 seconds.
About 14 seconds is the single-track time; a double track takes more than 15.
GK11-q02-fwuwqc: 10 feet is too close; with no stop line, stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail.
20 to 100 feet isn't the rule; stop no closer than 15 and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail.
GK11-q03-n5j2rn: The X-shaped crossbuck marks the crossing itself and means yield; the round sign stands before it.
The round sign doesn't mean gates; it warns a crossing is ahead: slow down, look, listen.
GK11-q04-6lqnx7: High ground clearance is the opposite of the problem; low-slung units are the ones that hang up.
The listed risk is a single-axle tractor with a long trailer set for a tandem, not this setup.
GK11-q05-5c8ji4: Don't try to save the truck; get out and well away from the tracks first.
Never wait in the cab; leave the vehicle, get well away from the tracks, then call 9-1-1.
GK11-q06-svtc08: Don't change gears on the tracks; a missed shift could leave you stalled there.
Upshifting is still a gear change; a missed shift could leave you stalled on the tracks.
GK11-q07-isbcge: Wait until the gates are all the way up and the lights stop flashing, not just until the train clears.
Never go around a gate; stay stopped until the gates are up and the lights stop flashing.
GK11-q08-gxcbzv: A train on one track can hide a train on the other; check both ways before starting.
Look both ways; a second train could be coming from either direction on the other track.
GK11-q09-8kfpwv: Steepness of the grade is one of the five safe-speed factors.
Total weight of the vehicle and cargo is one of the five safe-speed factors.
GK11-q10-ks16oa: Too late; once speed builds you may not get into any gear and lose all engine braking.
Downshifting after speed builds may fail, leaving you in no gear with no engine braking.
GK11-q11-3xtcsh: Same gear down as up is the older-truck rule; modern trucks may need a lower gear.
Modern trucks have less friction and drag going down, so they may need a lower gear, not higher.
GK11-q12-7bmygw: Don't let speed pass your safe speed; brake at 45 and release about 5 mph below, at 40.
Steady light braking builds heat and causes fade; use firm applications, release, and repeat.
GK11-q13-6yijx8: One second is too short; each firm application should last about 3 seconds.
Ten seconds is too long and builds heat; each application should last about 3 seconds.
GK11-q14-fb0irw: The service brakes are only a supplement on a downgrade; engine braking is the main control.
The trailer hand valve is for testing trailer brakes, not driving; engine braking is the main control.
GK11-q15-g7kpz4: Grabbing and pulling to one side is a wet-brake problem, not brake fade.
Low air pressure is a different problem; fade is overheated brakes needing more and more pressure.
GK11-q16-1uu6ib: Out-of-adjustment brakes do less work, not more; the others then overheat and fade.
Adjustment affects every brake; the out-of-adjustment ones quit first and the rest overheat.
GK11-q17-kspe5m: Escape ramps aren't rest stops; they stop runaway vehicles in a long bed of loose, soft material.
Escape ramps aren't for letting traffic pass; they are built to stop runaway vehicles safely.
GK11-dn-vuml2a: Flashing red lights make a crossing active; a passive crossing has no traffic control device.
Gates make a crossing active; a passive crossing has no device, so the decision is yours.
GK11-dn-1lo9qa: A crossbuck only marks the crossing; an active crossing has flashing red lights, or lights with gates.
Pavement markings only warn of a crossing ahead; an active crossing has flashing lights or gates.
GK11-dn-basgmy: The X-shaped sign is the crossbuck, which marks the crossing itself.
The painted X and RR is the pavement marking, which carries the same message as the sign.
GK11-dn-cw8p6s: Not only school buses; all vehicles carrying passengers or HazMat must stop.
Pulling a trailer doesn't trigger the stop; the rule covers vehicles carrying passengers or HazMat.
GK11-dn-764i9y: The marking doesn't order a full stop; like the advance sign, it means slow down, look, listen, be ready.
Pavement markings don't signal gates; they carry the advance warning sign's message.
GK11-dn-ir9rh3: The sign below the crossbuck shows how many tracks there are, not train speed.
The sign below the crossbuck shows the number of tracks, not a distance.
GK11-dn-jjzz4j: Too close is dangerous; with no stop line, stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail.
The distance is measured from the nearest rail of the nearest track, not from the crossbuck.
GK11-dn-wufyar: With no stop line you stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest rail, not as close as possible.
Drivers behind may not expect you to stop; check behind and stop gradually, not quickly.
GK11-dn-kk2km1: Three seconds is the length of a downhill brake application, not a track-clearing time.
More than 15 seconds is the double-track figure.
GK11-dn-56uwph: About 14 seconds is the single-track figure; a double track takes more than 15.
Three seconds is a downhill brake-application time, far too short to clear any track.
GK11-dn-oqyd9y: Landing gear set for a tandem suits a tandem tractor; the risk is pairing it with a single-axle tractor.
High ground clearance is the opposite of the problem; low-riding rigs are the ones that hang up.
GK11-dn-wfe4jz: Your CDL number doesn't help responders; give the crossing's location, especially the DOT number.
Train length isn't what's asked; give the crossing's location, especially its posted DOT number.
GK11-dn-57li1b: Traffic speed and time of day aren't factors; the list is weight, length, steepness, road conditions, weather.
Engine power isn't a factor; the first one is the total weight of vehicle and cargo.
GK11-dn-7p9al4: It's the reverse: engine braking is strongest near governed rpm with the transmission in a lower gear.
Service brakes are separate from engine braking, which peaks near governed rpm in lower gears.
GK11-dn-mda7bb: 10 mph below is too much; brake to about 5 mph below your safe speed, then release.
15 mph below is too much; brake to about 5 mph below your safe speed, then release.
GK11-dn-cayfyt: 14 seconds is the time to clear a single railroad track, not a brake application.
More than 15 seconds is the time to clear a double railroad track, not a brake application.
GK11-dn-rr9z12: Never let speed rise above your safe speed; start braking when you reach 40 mph.
Steady light braking builds heat and causes fade; brake firmly, release, and repeat.
